blocks.content: The ultimate power of passing an ordinary bill resides with the Legislative Assembly, and the Legislative Council can at most delay its passage.

rows: Either Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council
Can amend, reject, or delay up to 4 months
Cannot amend or reject; can delay max 14 days
Assembly overrides Council; no joint sitting
Assembly overrides Council; no joint sitting

items: There is NO provision for a joint sitting of both Houses of the State Legislature to resolve a deadlock over a bill, unlike at the Union level.
The Legislative Assembly can override the Legislative Council's amendments or rejection of an ordinary bill by passing it a second time.
When a bill is reserved by the Governor for the consideration of the President, the Governor drops out of the legislative process and has no further role.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: An ordinary bill can originate in either the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a state.
The Legislative Council possesses only suspensive delay powers and can delay an ordinary bill for a maximum period of 4 months (3 months in the first instance and 1 month in the second instance).
A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly and only on the prior recommendation of the Governor.
The Legislative Council has no power to reject or amend a Money Bill and must return it within 14 days with or without recommendations.

Under Article 200, when a bill is passed by the state legislature, the Governor can give assent, withhold assent, return the bill for reconsideration, or reserve it for the consideration of the President.
